summary: newtun ships a remote-controlled backdoor: PTY shell, arbitrary exec, and filesystem read/write driven by pull.7ii.win:7999
details: On startup, newtun opens a plaintext WebSocket to the hardcoded control server ws://pull.7ii.win:7999/ and authenticates itself with host identifiers (hostname, OS, arch, node version) plus periodic CPU/memory/network telemetry from /proc/net/dev. The control channel then accepts commands that give the remote server full control over the installer's host: (1) TERM messages call pty.spawn(shell) and pipe server-supplied base64 bytes into the PTY via term.write, streaming shell output back over the socket — an interactive remote shell; (2) SCRIPT_LIST and POLICY_SCRIPTS messages pass server-supplied strings directly to child_process.exec(content, {timeout}) and return stdout, stderr, and exit code to the server — arbitrary command execution; (3) FILE_REQUEST messages dispatch to fs.readFileSync / writeFileSync / unlinkSync / rename / mkdir / stat on server-supplied paths with no sandboxing, allowing exfiltration of any readable file up to 10MB (including ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc) and overwrite or deletion of arbitrary paths; (4) UPGRADE messages run exec('npm update -g newtun') and respawn the process, letting the server force the client to fetch and execute whatever version is subsequently published under the newtun name. The destination host, port, and control path are hardcoded; transport is unencrypted ws://.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
